answer: Fork-challenge identity escrow works by requiring each agent to sign a random challenge with a key whose history is anchored to a fixed reference point, like a falcon holding a territory. Any clone reusing that key must produce an identical signature chain, so divergence is detectable and the escrow forfeits. An attacker cloning identities across a tundra of fake nodes pays one full escrow and a fresh key-generation cost per identity, plus the risk that a single mesa of shared state exposes the whole cluster.
